1.q: PRINCE2 Agile describes a project in terms of three broad areas of work and aims to cover all of them while keeping governance and control throughout. Which three areas are these?
o: Project direction, project management and product delivery
Business justification, project management and service transition
Project direction, team leadership and benefits realization
Portfolio direction, project management and operational support
1.w: The book divides a project into project direction, project management and product delivery. PRINCE2 Agile covers all three, keeping governance and control in place throughout (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 3.1, Figure 3.1).

n.1: Service transition is not one of the three areas; the book names direction, management and product delivery (3.1).
n.2: Team leadership and benefits realization are not the named areas; the third area is product delivery, where agile is strongest (3.1).
n.3: The first area is project direction, not portfolio direction, and operational support belongs to BAU rather than the three project areas (3.1).

1.q: A delivery team at a regional water company keeps its requirements in a backlog. How does PRINCE2 Agile define a backlog?
o: A prioritized list of the requirements for a product, which may be epics or user stories
A record of the risks and issues the team has raised during the current iteration
A visual plan that groups user stories into releases of two to four iterations
A one-page summary of the project's vision, value, costs, benefits and major risks
1.w: In the PRINCE2 Agile glossary a backlog is a prioritized list of requirements for a product, and the items can be epic user stories, user stories or other requirement formats (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, Glossary).

n.1: Risks and issues are recorded in the risk register and issue register; a backlog holds requirements, not risks and issues (book 10.3.2, Glossary).
n.2: Grouping user stories into releases of two to four iterations describes the release map, which is the project and stage plan (book 8.3.2.5).
n.3: A one-page summary of vision, value, costs, benefits and risks is the project canvas, the agile form of the business case (book 6.3.2.1).

1.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, what does 'being agile' mean?
o: Applying agile frameworks, following agile processes and techniques, and adopting agile terminology in the team
Thinking in an agile way and being allowed to apply that mindset to work within suitable levels of self-management
Holding recognized agile certifications and using the vocabulary of a chosen framework in daily team work
Following the events and artifacts of one agile framework closely so that every team works in the same way
1.w: Being agile combines an agile way of thinking with permission to apply it to your work within appropriate self-management. Thinking alone is not enough if people are not allowed to act on it (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3.1).

n.0: This is the definition of 'doing agile': the practical application of frameworks, processes, techniques and terminology (book 2.3.1).
n.2: Certifications and framework vocabulary sit on the 'doing' side (terminology); being agile is a way of thinking plus the freedom to apply it (book 2.3.1).
n.3: Following a framework closely is doing agile, and following it rigidly without knowing why is the 'routine' side of the contrast (book 2.3.1).

1.q: A housing association runs a repairs helpdesk that answers tenant calls every day of the year. It also sets up a team to replace its tenant records system by next spring. Which characteristic of the second piece of work shows that it is a project rather than business as usual?
o: It uses staff with specialist technical and engineering skills
It must be delivered within a budget agreed by senior managers
It has a defined start and end, after which BAU adopts the change
It serves the association's tenants and responds to their needs
1.w: Temporary is one of the five characteristics that distinguish a project from business as usual: a project has a start and an end, after which BAU takes on the change and the benefits follow. The helpdesk runs indefinitely, so it is BAU (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.1).

n.0: Specialist skills are used in both pieces of work, so they do not set the project apart from the helpdesk; skills are not one of the project characteristics (book 1.3.1).
n.1: BAU operations such as the helpdesk also run to budgets, so a budget does not distinguish a project from BAU (book 1.3.1).
n.3: Both the helpdesk and the new system serve tenants, so serving customers is not what makes the second piece of work a project (book 1.3.1).

1.q: PRINCE2 Project Management, on which PRINCE2 Agile builds, is made up of five integrated elements. Which element covers the needs, capabilities and motivations of those involved in a project and the relationships between them?
o: People
Principles
Project context
Practices
1.w: People is the integrated element concerned with the needs, capabilities and motivations of everyone involved and the relationships between them; it sits at the centre of the method (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2, summarized in PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.1).

n.1: The principles are the guiding obligations and good practices that decide whether a project is genuinely PRINCE2; they do not describe people's needs and relationships (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2).
n.2: The project context is the setting the method is applied in, such as the organizational and commercial context, delivery method and scale (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2).
n.3: The practices are the seven aspects of project management, such as business case and risk, applied throughout the lifecycle (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2).

1.q: Which PRINCE2 Agile practice provides the mechanisms for judging whether a project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable, as a basis for decisions about continued investment?
o: Business case
Progress
Organization
Risk
1.w: The business case practice exists to establish mechanisms for judging whether the project is (and stays) desirable, viable and achievable, which supports decisions on continued investment (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.1).

n.1: Progress monitors actual achievement against plan and forecasts continued viability, but judging desirability, viability and achievability for investment decisions is the business case purpose (book 12.1, 6.1).
n.2: Organization establishes the structure of accountability and responsibilities; it decides who takes investment decisions, not whether the investment is justified (book 7.1).
n.3: Risk identifies, assesses and controls uncertainty that could affect objectives; it does not provide the overall judgement of desirability, viability and achievability (book 10.1).

1.q: A new sponsor asks what the organization practice contributes to a PRINCE2 Agile project. Which statement describes the purpose of the organization practice?
o: To define and establish the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities
To control changes to the project's baseline once the project backlog has been agreed
To compare actual achievements with those planned and forecast the project's objectives
To document the users' requirements of the project products and how they will be met
1.w: The organization practice answers the 'who' question: it defines and establishes the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 7.1; practice purposes 6.1 to 12.1, paraphrased).

n.1: Controlling changes to the baseline is the purpose of the issues practice, not organization.
n.2: Comparing actual against planned achievement and forecasting objectives is the purpose of the progress practice.
n.3: Documenting users' requirements and the means of meeting them is the purpose of the quality practice.

1.q: A new delivery team starts work, measures how much it completes in each iteration and uses that rate to forecast when the release will be finished. Which term does PRINCE2 Agile use for basing planning decisions on this kind of experience?
o: Rationalism
Empiricism
Timeboxing
Decomposition
1.w: Empiricism means making decisions from experience, meaning what is happening or has already happened: start the work, see how much gets done and forecast from that (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3).

n.0: Rationalism is the opposite of empiricism: it relies on reasoning and logic to predict and plan before evidence exists (book 8.3).
n.2: Timeboxing fixes the length of a period of work (iteration, release or stage); it does not describe forecasting from observed progress (Glossary).
n.3: Decomposition is breaking work into smaller parts, as a story map does; it is not the term for planning from experience (book 8.3.1).

1.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, what provides the starting point that drives the quality practice?
o: The lessons recorded in the project log
The requirements held in the project backlog
The tolerances shown on the project dashboard
The risk responses recorded in the risk register
1.w: In an agile context the quality practice is driven by the requirements in the project backlog, which replaces the project product description (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.3.1, 8.3.2.1).

n.0: The project log (daily and lessons log) supports the progress practice; it does not define what the products must be like (book Table 12.1).
n.2: The project dashboard reports progress to the board (it replaces the highlight report); it does not set the quality requirements (book Table 12.1).
n.3: Risk responses belong to the risk practice; quality starts from what the users require, held in the project backlog (book 10.3, 9.3.1).

1.q: A project manager at a regional bus operator is explaining to new team members how risk will be handled across the iterations. PRINCE2 Agile recommends adapting the PRINCE2 Project Management risk technique. Which sequence lists the steps of that technique?
o: Capture, assess, recommend, decide, implement
Identify, assess, plan, implement, review
Identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate
Identify, plan, assess, communicate, implement
1.w: PRINCE2 Agile adapts the five-step PRINCE2 Project Management risk technique: identify, assess, plan, implement and communicate, woven into the iteration cycle (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 10.3.1, Figure 10.1).

n.0: Capture, assess, recommend, decide and implement are the steps of the issues technique (PRINCE2 7 manual 10.3.1), not the risk technique adapted in PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 10.3.1.
n.1: The fifth step of the risk technique is communicate, not review; communication runs through the established feedback loops of the iterations (book 10.3.1, Figure 10.1).
n.3: Risks must be assessed (estimated and evaluated) before responses are planned, and implement comes before communicate in the technique (book 10.3.1, Figure 10.1).

1.q: A project manager new to PRINCE2 Agile asks what the progress practice is for. Which statement describes its purpose?
o: To identify, assess and control uncertainties that would affect the project's objectives
To collect and assess issues and control changes to the project's baseline
To compare actual achievements with plans and forecast the project's objectives and viability
To document the users' requirements and establish how they will be met
1.w: The progress practice monitors and compares actual achievements against those planned, forecasts the project's objectives and continued viability, and controls any deviation that would cause an exception (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.1).

n.0: This is the purpose of the risk practice, which deals with uncertainty rather than tracking achievement against plan (book chapter 10).
n.1: This is the purpose of the issues practice, which handles issues and controls changes to the baseline (book 11.1).
n.3: This is the purpose of the quality practice, which sets out what users need and how it will be achieved (book Table 9.1).

1.q: A housing association has received a project mandate for a new tenant repairs app. Before any initiation work is authorized, the board wants to know whether there is a viable and worthwhile project at all. Which process has the purpose of answering this question?
o: Initiating a project
Starting up a project
Directing a project
Managing a stage boundary
1.w: Starting up a project makes sure the prerequisites for initiating are in place by answering whether there is a viable and worthwhile project; it is triggered by the project mandate (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.2.1).

n.0: Initiating a project comes after starting up; it lays solid foundations so the business understands the work before committing significant expenditure (book 13.4.1).
n.2: Directing a project lets the board stay accountable through key decisions; the question of whether there is a viable and worthwhile project is the purpose of starting up (book 13.3.1).
n.3: Managing a stage boundary gives the board information to review the current stage and approve the next stage plan; it is not where the first viability question is asked (book 13.7.1).

1.q: PRINCE2 Agile compares the strengths of traditional project management with those of agile ways of working. Which statement reflects that comparison?
o: Project management is strong on product delivery, while agile is strong on governance and control
Project management and agile are equally strong across direction, management and delivery
Agile is strong on project direction, while project management is strong on responding to change
Project management is strong on governance and control, while agile is strong on product delivery
1.w: Project management brings governance and control but says little about product delivery; agile is strong on product delivery and responding to change but light on direction and management. Blending them covers both (book 3.1).

n.0: This reverses the comparison: product delivery is agile's strength and governance is project management's (3.1).
n.1: They are not equally strong; each has gaps, which is why the book blends them (3.1).
n.2: Agile is light on direction and management, and responding to change is an agile strength, not a project management one (3.1).

1.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, several management products are tailored into agile artifacts. Which management product does the project backlog replace?
o: The product description for each team's products
The project product description
The project brief
The stage plan for the current stage
1.w: The project backlog is the PRINCE2 Agile tailoring of the project product description: a high-level backlog, mostly of epics, that shows or links to the project DoR and DoD and names who accepts the project product (book 8.3.2.1).

n.0: Product descriptions at team level are replaced by each team's product backlog, not by the project backlog (book 8.3.2.1).
n.2: The project brief remains a business case product in PRINCE2 Agile, outlining flexible scope and quality areas; it is not replaced by the project backlog (book Table 6.1).
n.3: The stage plan, like the project plan, takes the form of a release map, not the project backlog (book 8.3.2.5).

1.q: Which description matches 'doing agile' in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: A way of thinking that people are free to apply within agreed levels of self-management
A cultural shift in the organization that builds long-term resilience and adaptability
The belief that any person can learn, adapt to change and grow over time
The practical application of agile frameworks, processes, techniques and terminology
1.w: Doing agile is the hands-on use of agile frameworks, processes and techniques and the adoption of agile terminology (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3.1).

n.0: Thinking in an agile way with freedom to apply it is 'being agile', not doing agile (book 2.3.1).
n.1: Cultural shift and long-term resilience are what being agile brings; doing agile alone gives short-term gains (book 2.3.1).
n.2: This is the growth mindset, often seen as the core of the agile mindset, not doing agile (book 2.6.1, 2.7.3).

1.q: A hospital trust forms a team to introduce electronic prescribing. The team includes pharmacists, ward nurses, IT staff and engineers from an external software company. Which characteristic of a project does this team composition illustrate?
o: The project is cross-functional
The project is unique
The project is temporary
The project introduces change
1.w: Cross-functional: project teams work across the functional divisions of BAU and sometimes span different organizations, as here with several departments and an external supplier (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.1).

n.1: Unique is about a project differing from others, for example in team, customer, supplier, location or timeframe; the stem describes who is in the team, not how the project differs (book 1.3.1).
n.2: Temporary is about the project having a start and an end; nothing in the stem concerns its duration (book 1.3.1).
n.3: Change is about BAU identifying a need and the project introducing it; the stem is about the mix of people, not the change itself (book 1.3.1).

1.q: Which group does the people element of PRINCE2 Project Management cover?
o: The project board and the project manager, who hold the formal decision-making roles
Both the people working on the project and the people affected by what it delivers
The delivery teams, because they create the products the project hands over
The users who will operate the new system once it is released into service
1.w: The people element covers those working on the project and those affected by it, such as staff in the business who must integrate the new products into their area (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2 and 3.1, PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.1).

n.0: Board members and the project manager are part of the people element, but it also reaches every other team member and everyone affected by the project (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.1).
n.2: Delivery teams are inside the project team, but the element also covers the governance roles and the people affected by the change (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.1).
n.3: Future users are among the people affected, but the element also covers everyone working on the project (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2).

1.q: What is the purpose of the organization practice in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: To collect and assess issues and to control changes to the project's baseline
To define and establish the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities
To define the products to be delivered and the means by which they will be delivered
To monitor and compare actual achievements against those planned
1.w: The organization practice defines and establishes the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities, in other words who does what (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 7.1).

n.0: Collecting and assessing issues and controlling baseline changes is the purpose of the issues practice (book 11.1).
n.2: Defining the products and the means of delivering them is the purpose of the plans practice (book 8.1).
n.3: Monitoring and comparing actual against planned achievement is part of the purpose of the progress practice (book 12.1).

1.q: A product owner on a PRINCE2 Agile project asks where they sit in the project management team structure. Which role has the direct line of authority over the product owner?
o: The chief product owner, who sets priorities across the teams
The project manager, who runs the project day to day for the board
The team coach, who supports the product owner and the team
The agile coach, who advises the board on agile ways of working
1.w: In the PRINCE2 Agile structure (book Figure 7.1, Table 7.2) the project manager is the role with the direct line of authority over the product owner. The PO is a version of the team manager role and agrees work with the PM.

n.0: The CPO works closely with product owners and sets priorities across teams, but the structure does not give the CPO the line of authority over the PO.
n.2: The team coach supports and advises the PO and the delivery team; it holds no line authority over the PO.
n.3: The agile coach supports the board, project assurance and the PM at organization level; it is not in the PO's line of authority.

1.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.

Starting the work and then seeing how much a team actually gets done is sometimes called [?], by comparison with setting a pair of weighing scales to zero before using them.
o: calibration
refactoring
baselining
swarming
1.w: The plans practice describes starting work to see the real rate of progress as calibration, likened to zeroing scales, or as calculating velocity (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3).

n.1: Refactoring is improving the internal structure of a product without changing its behaviour; it is not a way of measuring the team's rate.
n.2: Baselining fixes an approved version of a product or plan for control purposes; the book's term for measuring the team's real rate is calibration (book 8.3).
n.3: Swarming is the whole team focusing on one item, often a blocker; it is not about measuring how much gets done.

2.q: Which cycle does the quality practice follow in PRINCE2 Agile to align the project products with the quality management approach?
o: Identify, assess, plan, implement and communicate
Develop, check, maintain and confirm
Capture, assess, recommend, decide and implement changes
Quality planning, quality control and product acceptance
2.w: The quality practice aligns the project products with the quality management approach through a cycle of quality planning, quality control and product acceptance (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.3.1).

n.0: These are the five steps of the risk management technique in the risk practice, not the quality cycle (book 10.3.1).
n.1: These steps describe how the business case is handled over the life of the project, not how quality is managed (book ch 6).
n.2: These are the steps of the issue management technique in the issues practice, used to control changes to the baseline (book 11.3; PRINCE2 7 issue technique).

2.q: A delivery team at an online furniture retailer works in two-week iterations. According to PRINCE2 Agile, where is the 'identify' step of the risk technique suggested to be a fixed part of the team's routine?
o: In every planning session and in every team and project retrospective
In the project kickoff workshop, held once while the project is initiated
In the project closure workshop, when lessons for future projects are recorded
In the project board's review of each exception report from the manager
2.w: The identify step is suggested to be a fixed part of every planning session and of team and project retrospectives, where risks are gathered and documented. Risks can still be raised at any other time (book 10.3.1, Figure 10.1).

n.1: The kickoff workshop builds teamwork, values and dashboards; a one-off workshop cannot be the fixed, recurring place for identifying risks (book Table 13.8, 10.3.1).
n.2: The closure workshop confirms the product, records lessons and prepares handover; identifying project risks there is far too late to act on them (book 13.8.4, 10.3.1).
n.3: Exception reports deal with forecast tolerance breaches; the book places risk identification in the team's planning sessions and retrospectives (book 10.3.1, Table 12.1).

2.q: According to the progress practice, which aspect of performance is usually of most interest to the whole project management team, making burn charts a natural choice at any level of the project?
o: Flexibility in what is delivered
Spend measured against the budget
Time used against the time tolerance
Hours logged against each team task
2.w: The book treats flexibility in what is delivered as probably the primary performance aspect of interest to the whole project management team, so showing it on burn charts suits any project level (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.3.1).

n.1: Cost has zero tolerance on all levels of plan in PRINCE2 Agile, so there is little point tracking spend against budget as the main measure (book 12.3.1, Table 3.1).
n.2: Time also has zero tolerance on all levels of plan, so tracking use of a time tolerance tells the team little (book 12.3.1, Table 3.1).
n.3: Agile estimating is relative (for example story points), and progress is shown by what is delivered, not by hours logged on tasks (book 8.4.3, 12.3.1).

2.q: Which statement describes the purpose of the 'initiating a project' process in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: To check that the prerequisites for initiation are in place by confirming the project is viable and worthwhile
To give the board enough information to review the current stage and approve the plan for the next stage
To control the link between the project manager and the delivery team for the delivery of specialist products
To establish solid foundations so the business understands the work needed before committing significant expenditure
2.w: Initiating a project establishes solid foundations so the business understands the work needed to deliver the project product before committing to significant expenditure (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.4.1).

n.0: This is the purpose of starting up a project, which comes before initiation and asks whether the project is viable and worthwhile (book 13.2.1).
n.1: This is the purpose of managing a stage boundary, which supports the board's review of each stage (book 13.7.1).
n.2: This is the purpose of managing product delivery, which links the project manager with the delivery team (book 13.6.1).

2.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In PRINCE2 Agile Version 2, business case, organization, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress are described as the seven [?].
o: themes
practices
processes
aspects
2.w: Version 2 follows PRINCE2 7 and calls these seven elements practices; the old word 'themes' is no longer used (Agile V2 syllabus 2.1.2; book chapters 6 to 12, one per practice).

n.0: 'Themes' is the term from the 6th edition and PRINCE2 Agile Version 1; V2 calls them practices.
n.2: The seven processes are starting up, directing, initiating, controlling a stage, managing product delivery, managing a stage boundary and closing, not these seven.
n.3: The seven aspects of performance are benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk, not this list.

2.q: A product owner would traditionally send checkpoint reports to the project manager. In PRINCE2 Agile, which artifact takes the place of the checkpoint report?
o: The project dashboard
The release map
The team dashboard
The product backlog
2.w: The team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report. It is updated and reviewed in team planning and retrospective workshops, and the project manager pulls progress information from it (book Table 12.1).

n.0: The project dashboard replaces the highlight report and end stage report, used by the board, not the checkpoint report (book Table 12.1).
n.1: The release map is the agile form of the project and stage plans; it is a plan, not a progress report from the team (book 8.3.2.5).
n.3: The product backlog replaces product descriptions and holds the team's user stories; it does not report progress to the project manager (book 8.3.2.1).

2.q: PRINCE2 Agile contrasts being agile and doing agile under the heading 'adaptability versus routine'. Which statement reflects this contrast?
o: Being agile lets teams adapt and think critically, while doing agile alone may mean following a framework rigidly without knowing why
Doing agile lets teams adapt and think critically, while being agile alone may leave them following routines with no structure
Being agile delivers short-term efficiency gains, while doing agile creates a lasting cultural shift in the organization
Doing agile relies on stable routines suited to business as usual, while being agile is reserved for project work
2.w: Under 'adaptability versus routine', being agile allows teams to adapt to change and think critically, whereas doing agile on its own can leave them applying a framework rigidly without understanding the reasons (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3.1).

n.1: This reverses the contrast: it is being agile that supports adaptation and critical thinking (book 2.3.1).
n.2: This reverses the 'long-term impact versus short-term mechanics' contrast: doing agile alone gives short-term gains (book 2.3.1).
n.3: The contrast is about mindset versus mechanics, not about splitting agile between business as usual and projects; agile is used in both (book 2.3.1, 1.1).

2.q: Which statement describes project management, as defined in PRINCE2 Project Management and used in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: The running of business as usual operations within agreed service levels
The agreed limits within which a manager may act before escalating
The expected success level against which a project's management is judged
Applying methods, tools, techniques and competencies to meet project objectives
2.w: Project management is the application of methods, tools, techniques and competencies to a project so that it meets its objectives (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.2).

n.0: Running day-to-day operations is business as usual, which projects change; it is not project management (book 1.3.1).
n.1: Agreed limits of authority before escalation describe tolerances under the 'manage by exception' principle, not project management (book 5.2.1.5).
n.2: The expected success level against which management of the project is judged is the definition of a performance target, not of project management (book 1.3.2).

2.q:
Identify the missing words in the following sentence.

PRINCE2 Project Management contrasts the existing organizational ecosystem of business, users and suppliers with the [?], which is the temporary set of people, relationships, structures and ways of working set up for the project.
o: business layer
project management team structure
project ecosystem
delivery team
2.w: The project ecosystem is temporary and created for the project, where the business, user and supplier interests meet; the organizational ecosystem is what already exists (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.1).

n.0: The business layer is the permanent commissioning level outside the project; it is part of the existing organizational ecosystem (PRINCE2 7 manual ch 6).
n.1: The project management team structure is a management product showing roles and reporting lines, not the wider set of relationships and ways of working (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 7.3.2).
n.3: A delivery team is one group inside the project; the temporary whole that includes relationships and ways of working is the project ecosystem (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.1).

2.q: Which practice exists to document the users' requirements of the project products and to establish the means by which those requirements will be met?
o: Plans
Business case
Quality
Issues
2.w: The quality practice documents users' requirements of the project products and establishes how they will be met, answering what is acceptable to users and how it can be measured (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.1, Table 5.2).

n.0: Plans define the products to be delivered and the who, how, where, when and how much of delivering them; users' quality requirements belong to the quality practice (book 8.1).
n.1: The business case judges whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable; it does not document users' requirements of the products (book 6.1).
n.3: Issues collects and assesses issues and controls changes to the baseline; it does not set out the users' requirements in the first place (book 11.1).

2.q: In a PRINCE2 Agile project, a delivery team is made up of a product owner, a team coach, developers and testers. Which role has the direct line of authority over the developers and testers?
o: The project manager, through the work packages
The team coach, through the team's workshops
The product owner of that delivery team
The senior supplier, through supplier resources
2.w: The product owner, a version of the team manager role, is the role with the direct line of authority over delivery team members (book Figure 7.1, Table 7.2). The PM works through the PO rather than directly with team members.

n.0: The project manager's direct authority is over the product owner; the PM does not manage developers and testers directly.
n.1: The team coach helps the team self-manage and facilitates its workshops but has no line authority over team members.
n.3: The senior supplier represents the supplier side at governance level; the structure places the delivery team members under the product owner.

2.q: Which statement describes the approach that the PRINCE2 Agile plans practice treats as the opposite of empiricism?
o: Iterative delivery, releasing the product in small increments
Self-management, where the team organizes its own work
Just-in-time planning of tasks for the next iteration
Rationalism, predicting and planning by reasoning and logic
2.w: The book contrasts empiricism, deciding from what is happening or has happened, with rationalism, which uses reasoning or logic to predict and plan (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3).

n.0: Iterative and incremental delivery is how agile teams deliver; it works alongside empirical planning rather than being its opposite (book 8.3).
n.1: Self-management describes how delivery teams organize their work; it is an agile characteristic, not the opposite of empiricism (book 2.6.2).
n.2: Planning task detail just in time for the next iteration is part of empirical agile planning, not its opposite (book 8.3.2.5).

2.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.

The question the quality practice answers in an agile project is what is [?] to the users and how this can be measured.
o: affordable
acceptable
achievable
desirable
2.w: The quality practice asks what is acceptable to the users and how that can be measured, which is why acceptance criteria and the DoD matter so much (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 5.2).

n.0: Whether the project is affordable is a viability question for the business case practice, not the quality question (book 6.1).
n.2: Achievability is also a business case test of whether the project should continue; quality asks what the users will accept (book 6.1, Table 5.2).
n.3: Desirability is one of the three tests (desirable, viable, achievable) applied by the business case practice (book 6.1).

2.q: At a garden-centre chain, a delivery team has gathered and documented several new risks during its retrospective. The team now estimates the probability and impact of each risk and evaluates them against one another. Which step of the risk technique is the team carrying out?
o: Identify
Plan
Implement
Assess
2.w: In the assess step, risks are estimated and evaluated. Estimating probability and impact and comparing the risks is assessment (book 10.3.1, Figure 10.1).

n.0: Identify is where risks are gathered and documented, which the team has already done in its retrospective (book 10.3.1, Figure 10.1).
n.1: Plan is where the necessary risk responses are planned; the team is still estimating and evaluating the risks (book 10.3.1, Figure 10.1).
n.2: Implement is where planned responses are carried out within the iteration cycle; no responses have been chosen yet (book 10.3.1, Figure 10.1).

2.q: A team coach wants a chart for the daily stand-up that shows how many story points of work are still outstanding on each day of the current iteration. Which technique fits best?
o: A burn-up chart
A burn-down chart
A cumulative risk burn-down chart
A cumulative flow diagram
2.w: A burn-down chart is a run chart of outstanding work over time, typically used at team level to show story points over the days of an iteration (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.4.3).

n.0: A burn-up chart plots completed work against a deadline and is typically used at project or product level across stages or iterations (book 12.4.3).
n.2: A cumulative risk burn-down chart shows the total risk exposure across iterations, not outstanding story points (book 10.4.2).
n.3: A cumulative flow diagram shows how many tasks sit in each workflow state over time to reveal bottlenecks; it is not a run chart of work remaining (book 12.4.2).

2.q: A delivery team and its project manager agree the requirements for accepting, carrying out, reporting on and delivering a set of user stories. Which process has the purpose of controlling this link between the project manager and the delivery team?
o: Managing product delivery
Controlling a stage
Directing a project
Managing a stage boundary
2.w: Managing product delivery controls the link between the project manager and the delivery team by agreeing requirements for acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery of specialist products (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.6.1).

n.1: Controlling a stage is the project manager's process for assigning and monitoring work and keeping the stage within tolerances; the team side of the link is managing product delivery (book 13.5.1).
n.2: Directing a project is the board's process for key decisions and overall control; it does not manage the project manager's link with the delivery team (book 13.3.1).
n.3: Managing a stage boundary prepares information for the board's review of the stage and the next stage plan; it does not control work packages (book 13.7.1).

2.q: Which statement BEST describes what PRINCE2 Agile is?
o: An agile delivery framework that replaces the PRINCE2 processes with Scrum events and roles
A version of PRINCE2 that drops whichever principles conflict with agile ways of working
PRINCE2 Project Management tailored with an agile mindset, frameworks, artifacts and workshops
A team-level method for product delivery that leaves project governance to BAU
2.w: PRINCE2 Agile keeps the PRINCE2 principles, practices and processes and tailors them with the agile mindset, agile frameworks, artifacts, techniques and workshops, so it covers direction, management and delivery (book 3.1).

n.0: The PRINCE2 processes stay; PRINCE2 Agile adds workshops to them and can work with Scrum or other frameworks (3.1).
n.1: No principle is dropped: all seven PRINCE2 principles apply, and only their application is tailored (5.2).
n.3: PRINCE2 Agile keeps governance and control throughout the project; it is not a team-level delivery method (3.1).

2.q: PRINCE2 Agile uses timeboxes at more than one level of a project. Which three levels of timebox does it define?
o: Sprint, iteration and release
Iteration, increment and project
Release, stage and project
Iteration, release and stage
2.w: A timebox is a fixed period of time, and PRINCE2 Agile names three levels of it: the iteration, the release and the stage (book Glossary).

n.0: Sprint is Scrum's name for an iteration, so it is not a separate level; the stage level is missing from this list (book Glossary).
n.1: An increment is a piece of product delivered, not a period of time, and the project is not one of the three timebox levels (book Glossary).
n.2: The project is not one of the named timebox levels, and the iteration, the shortest timebox, is missing (book Glossary).

2.q:
Identify the missing words in the following sentence.

If an organization labels its processes 'agile' but its people are not allowed to think and act in an agile way, there is a gap between [?] agile.
o: scaling and sustaining
planning and delivering
being and doing
valuing and practising
2.w: Calling processes agile means little if people are not permitted to think and act in an agile way; PRINCE2 Agile describes this as the gap between being and doing agile (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3).

n.0: Scaling and sustaining are separate topics (book 3.2, 2.7.5); the gap between labels and freedom to act is between being and doing agile (book 2.3).
n.1: Planning and delivering are activities in any project; the gap described is between mindset with freedom (being) and mechanics (doing) (book 2.3).
n.3: Values and practices are layers of the Agile Onion; the book names this gap as being versus doing agile (book 2.3, 2.6.1).

2.q: Which of the following best describes a project, as PRINCE2 Project Management defines the term?
o: A permanent team that runs and continually improves an organization's services
A temporary organization set up to deliver products under an agreed business case
A timeboxed period in which a delivery team builds and demonstrates user stories
A group of related initiatives managed together to achieve strategic outcomes
2.w: PRINCE2 defines a project as a temporary organization created to deliver one or more products according to an agreed business case (PRINCE2 Project Management 1.3; PRINCE2 Agile builds on this definition, book 1.3).

n.0: A permanent team running and improving services is business as usual; a project is temporary, with a start and an end (book 1.3.1).
n.2: A short timeboxed period in which a team builds and demonstrates stories is an iteration, one of the three timebox levels, not a project (PRINCE2 Agile Glossary).
n.3: A group of related initiatives managed together for strategic outcomes describes a programme or portfolio, which a project may form part of (book 1.3.4).
